title: Microjourney SDK tangible cheat catalog
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, tactile cheat catalog for the "microjourney" onboarding path — a 10–30 minute SDK experience aimed at engineers who want to evaluate Redwood in a minimal, instrumentable loop. It's intentionally light: copyable commands, one-file quickstarts, and a short checklist for telemetry and failure triage.

Audience:
- Engineers trying Redwood SDKs for the first time
- Solutions engineers preparing 15-minute demos
- Internal docs authors who want a minimal reproducible example to link from longer guides

Design principles (short):
- Minimal friction: a single file or two commands to see end-to-end behavior
- Observable by default: add telemetry probes and a smoke-check step in the happy-path script
- Repeatable: deterministic seed, clear env vars, explicit timeouts
- Safe defaults: short token limits, sandbox endpoints, noop webhooks

Quickstart (90s, copy-paste):
1) Create ephemeral env and install:
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_demo_xxx   # sandbox key
   - python -m venv .microvenv && source .microvenv/bin/activate
   - pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2
2) Run single-file sample (tiny_chat.py):
   - cat > tiny_chat.py <<'PY'
     from redwood import RedwoodClient
     c = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY", endpoint="https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai")
     r = c.chat.create(model="rwd-tiny-1", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Write a 3-line haiku about CI"}], max_tokens=64, timeout=6)
     print(r.output_text)
     PY
   - python tiny_chat.py
3) Run the smoke-check (telemetry):
   - curl -sS -X POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/telemetry/test -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"probe_id":"microjourney_happy_path","status":"ok"}'

Expected quick wins:
- A visible response printed within 2–6s
- Telemetry POST visible in the sandbox probe dashboard

One-file sample variants (tangible cheats):
- tiny_chat_logging.py: same as above but writes a JSON line with fields: request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out
- embed_small.py: generate embedding for a short string and show cosine similarity to a static vector (useful to demo retrieval integration)
- reranker_mini.py: submit 3 candidates and call rerank endpoint to show deterministic ordering changes

Smoke tests and gating checklist (run after any quickstart):
- ✅ API auth: token accepted (401/200)
- ✅ Latency: < 2s for tiny model, < 6s for small model on sandbox
- ✅ Determinism: same prompt + seed -> same output (when deterministic flag is set)
- ✅ Telemetry: at least one probe event with request_id and model tag
- ✅ Error handling: library returns non-2xx as structured exception with status code and error type

Telemetry probe keys (recommended minimal set):
- probe_id (string): microjourney_happy_path | microjourney_smoke_fail
- request_id (uuid)
- model (string)
- latency_ms (int)
- tokens_in, tokens_out (ints)
- error_class (optional string)
- sample_input_digest (sha1) — useful for prompt-regression attribution without storing PII

Failure modes we care about (and quick triage):
1) 401 / auth failure
   - Quick triage: check REDWOOD_API_KEY env, sandbox key expiry, IP allowlist
   - Probe: reproduce with curl and --verbose to confirm headers
2) Timeout / slow responses
   - Quick triage: increase timeout, switch to tiny model, compare latencies from different regions (if available)
   - Note: add a heatmap sample to telemetry after second run if above 2000ms
3) Determinism drift across SDK versions
   - Quick triage: pin SDK and server model versions, run same-seed test script and capture diffs to /tmp/microjourney-diff
4) JSON parse errors from structured responses
   - Quick triage: log raw response bytes; validate Content-Type; run local schema validation against the expected contract

Fallback matrix (minimal):
- If model unavailable -> auto-fallback to rwd-tiny-2 (configurable)
- If region/capacity issues -> return cached answer from last-successful-run (TTL 60s) and flag telemetry: fallback_used=true

Developer ergonomics heuristics (short):
- Provide a one-line curl equivalent for each SDK sample
- Keep sample prompts tiny (< 120 chars) and explicit about expected output shape
- Ship sample outputs (golden) to the repo for quick visual regression checks

Example troubleshooting session (scriptable):
- ./microjourney/check_session.sh 
  # does auth, minimal call, telemetry post, and grep for request_id
  # returns non-zero on any gate failure so CI can fail fast

Acceptance criteria for including a microjourney in the public quickstart gallery:
- reproduces in <= 30s on a laptop with an ephemeral sandbox key
- exposes at least 3 telemetry dimensions (request_id, latency_ms, model)
- includes a clear remediation step for each failure mode above
- README.md under sample directory with 3 lines explaining why the sample exists (what it proves)

Open TODOs (short):
- Decide whether to include automatic golden-output snapshotting in CI (risk: leaking prompts)
- Small set of deterministic seeds for each model family to use in regressions (assigned: Miguel)
- Add an offline-mode sample that simulates latency and returns cached outputs with TTLs (owner: Lin)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- Consider bundling "microjourney.box" — a tiny tarball with virtualenv and sample scripts for workshops
- Think about a single-step demo that shows: embed -> index (in-memory) -> retrieve -> rerank -> generate — compressed into <200 lines

If you copy this into a longer PRD or public quickstart, please: remove sandbox-specific keys, expand the telemetry section into a formal schema, and add a short paragraph about cost expectations for each sample.

Linked quick artifacts:
- "tiny_chat.py" and "tiny_chat_logging.py" belong in /sdk-examples/microjourney/ (create if missing)
- Quick demo checklist for SEs: paste the smoke checklist into the demo playbook (SE-runbook doc)

End of cheat catalog.
